amends.rule: the frozen file is not edited; this file records only what changed and why

trigger.content: askeladd E61 rung 1 closed M=7/8/9 for the single-stream form, priced the ceiling tax at -0.02 % to -0.06 % on untreated widths, and reframed m5_rbx as the M=5 dose point of an occupancy hypothesis
trigger.advisor_prediction: t55 (125 registers) and m5_rbx (90 registers) must time the SAME at M=5, because the register law is exact at NA=5 and there is no cliff to relieve

retractions.reason: measured on adjacent legs only; ledger 198 shows the same-binary null grows with leg separation (0.0032 % adjacent, 0.1147 % three apart, 0.1634 % five apart)
retractions.replacement: this session's own same-arm spread, taken at the widest separation the palindrome measures

retractions.reason: E61 rung 1 measured the +15-register table-maximum rise at -0.02 % / -0.06 % on untreated widths; the ceiling argument is dead
retractions.replacement: m5_rbx is retained purely as the M=5 dose point of the occupancy hypothesis

retractions.item: worker_low_memory_notices = 0 as evidence in rungs 2b and 3
retractions.reason: mtp-timed never forwards worker stderr, so the count could not be anything but zero

design.why_palindrome: every arm gets the same mean leg position, so linear thermal drift cancels to first order for every pairwise contrast, and the session measures its own same-arm null at separations 1, 3 and 5 for free
design.warmup_leg: leg 1 is discarded and excluded from the analysis; alphonse measured that a warm-up cuts the timed-leg entry-temperature spread from 13.53 C to 4.30 C
design.arm_order_constraint: t55 is measured before m5_rbx, so a session cut short still returns the shippable arm
design.cool_gate: real 40 C gate on every timed leg
design.estimator: time ~ arm + leg_position, ordinary least squares, base arm as reference

predictions.basis: rung 3 pair T2 measured the identical 125-vs-90 register contrast at the isolated M=5 cell: iso_m5_ipg5_r4 -> iso_m5_ipg5_rbx = +8.318 % +/- 1.007 %, so the 90-register form is SLOWER, not equal. Rung 3 R1 (-20.010 %) and N2 (-13.356 %) give the two cell wins whose 6.654 pp gap converts to -0.250 % at the leg through the 5.413 % M=5 QMV share.
predictions.third_outcome_the_advisor_did_not_enumer: a LOSS at M=5. If m5_rbx is slower at M=5 while t6_rbx is faster at M=6, the occupancy relief at M=6 is real but it is paid for out of an intrinsic row-block cost that M=5 measures directly. That makes rung 3 T2 the calibration constant for askeladd's arm rather than a contradiction of it.

decision_rule.tie_tolerance_raw_pct: this session's largest same-arm absolute leg spread at the widest separation the palindrome measures; conservative because it still carries the session drift
decision_rule.tie_tolerance_regression: |t| < 2.0 on the arm[t55] - arm[m5_rbx] contrast from time ~ arm + leg_position, which is the powered read
decision_rule.tie: advisor's occupancy hypothesis is supported at M=5
decision_rule.t55_faster: this prereg is supported; m5_rbx buys nothing at M=5 and rung 3 T2 generalises to the whole table
decision_rule.rbx_faster: both this prereg and rung 3 T2 are wrong at the leg level; the register story needs rebuilding
decision_rule.power_caveat: rung 3 resolved this same register contrast at the isolated cell with an 8x margin. The leg-level test dilutes it by the 5.413 % M=5 QMV share. If the measured contrast standard error exceeds half the predicted 0.250 % gap, a leg-level tie is UNDERPOWERED and must not be reported as support for the occupancy hypothesis. The verdict `t55_vs_rbx_test_is_powered` records this explicitly.
